findings.quote: but that in his whole strength and conduct he deserved to be stripped of power and punished
findings.problem: The Greek has a marked gap: ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ τὴν ῥώμην ὅλην* εἰς καθαίρεσιν τῆς ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐπιστροφῆς εἶναι καὶ κολάσεως. The text breaks off after ὅλην; 'and conduct' is invented and the sentence is smoothed over as if whole.
findings.proposed_fix: but that, in view of his whole power [text lost here], he was liable to removal from his rule, to correction, and to punishment

units.note: Minor, not flagged: ἀνατατικῶς means 'menacingly/threateningly', not 'strained'; this is lexical and the sense of bitter hostility is preserved. Also 'not only envoys but also his brother' adds an unneeded 'not only' to καὶ πέμψαντος ... μετὰ τῶν πρεσβευτῶν καὶ τὸν ἀδελφόν.

findings.quote: dealt with each as policy required in their interviews
findings.problem: Greek: τὴν προειρημένην δόξαν ἐνεργασάμενος ἑκάστοις κατὰ τὰς ἐντεύξεις, 'having produced in each of them, at the interviews, the impression already mentioned'. The English substitutes a different idea ('as policy required') and drops the reference back to the earlier-mentioned impression.
findings.proposed_fix: created in each of them, in their interviews, the impression already described

findings.problem: Greek: ἐκ τῆς Ἰσίνδης προσαγορευομένης πόλεως; the city is Isinda (people: Ἰσινδεῖς).

findings.quote: relieved the people of Sinda from the siege
findings.problem: Greek: τοὺς Ἰσινδεῖς ἐξελόμενος ἐκ τῆς πολιορκίας; the people of Isinda.
findings.proposed_fix: relieved the people of Isinda from the siege

units.note: Not flagged as stylistic/minor: 'taking leave with affected courtesy' renders ἀσπαζόμενον καὶ φιλοφρονούμενον ('greeting and treating her kindly'); sense of the story is unaffected.

findings.quote: In the affair concerning Ariarathes, the outcome became proverbial: though they had matters in hand, they came to grief at the hands of their enemies.
findings.problem: The Greek is fragmentary: ἐν... η... τῆς πράξεως τῆς περὶ τὸν Ἀριαράθην εἰς τὴν παροιμίαν: ἔχοντες γὰρ π... διετε... οι τοῖς πολεμίοις ἐγένοντο. Words are lost at the start, and in ἔχοντες γὰρ π... διετε... οι; the English reads as a complete sentence and supplies 'outcome' and 'came to grief', which are not in the surviving text.
findings.proposed_fix: [text lost] of the affair concerning Ariarathes [text lost] into the proverb; for having [text lost] they [text lost] fell to their enemies.

units.note: Greek is corrupt; the supplied fix only marks the gaps and does not restore the lost words.
